original_skills_acceptance.goal: Ship Relay 1.9 as the skills-runtime and creative-intelligence release: add a first-class relay.SKILLS system that discovers, validates, versions, resolves and loads portable expertise on demand, then use it to make Relay substantially stronger at aesthetic direction, interaction/flow, motion, platform-native UI craft and performance across web, macOS, Windows, Android and Linux/GNOME while expanding its engineering, GitHub and Cloudflare expertise without bloating the permanent MCP/tool surface.
original_skills_acceptance.acceptance: Release-facing metadata/docs identify Relay 1.9.0. Introduce a first-class skills registry/runtime with stable catalog/search/read/resolve/install-or-vendor/update/audit behavior and a manifest that records id/name/version/source, Relay-authored vs licensed-upstream vs private-project origin, license/provenance/source URL or repository+revision, integrity/hash, tags, dependencies, required/optional MCP capabilities, supported platforms, compatibility and update policy. Portable SKILL.md bundles may include references/scripts/assets, but untrusted executable content never gains ambient authority; validation, path containment, size/context budgets and dependency/capability checks fail closed. Skills are selected and loaded just-in-time from task intent/capability requirements rather than injected wholesale; resolution is deterministic/explainable and can report why a skill was chosen, rejected or unavailable. Add an upstream ingestion policy/pipeline that license-audits and pins redistributable skills instead of copying proprietary installed skills; preserve attribution and make update drift auditable. Creative priority packs cover aesthetic/art direction and anti-slop judgment, information architecture and interaction flow, design systems/tokens/components, motion/animation/microinteraction, visual-reference analysis and visual QA, plus platform-native guidance for web, macOS/SwiftUI, Windows/WinUI, Android/Material and Linux/GNOME/GTK/libadwaita. Figma-bound skills may orchestrate the real Figma MCP when present but must declare that dependency and degrade cleanly when absent; Relay does not counterfeit external tools. Performance/optimization is co-equal with creative quality: packs cover asset/image/font budgets, animation/compositor discipline, JS/CSS/runtime cost, rendering/hydration, network/cache/CDN strategy, Core Web Vitals or platform-equivalent profiling, and performance-aware visual effects; aesthetically ambitious output must carry explicit performance checks/budgets rather than disabling effects by default. Supporting packs cover build/frontend engineering, research/source-driven development, documentation, release engineering, testing/QA, accessibility and security; these are lower product priority for the current solo workflow but must provide a safe production baseline and be composable with creative packs. Expand GitHub skills around branch/PR/check/release/repository workflows and Cloudflare skills around Workers, builds/deployments, bindings, Access, cache/CDN/R2/browser/evidence flows, always reusing Relay's bounded SOURCE/CLOUD mutation primitives and exact-head/readback safety rather than bypassing them. Provide project-private skill overlays so Terra Prime/Field/other loew doctrine can extend general skills without forking upstream bundles. Add tests for manifest validation, provenance/license policy, deterministic resolution, JIT context limits, dependency/tool gating, hostile/pathological bundles, update/version drift and representative cross-pack composition. Existing Relay 1.8 contextual UI/progress contracts remain compatible. No giant prompt dump, no one-tool-per-skill explosion, no new standing credentials. Required install/tests, exact-head admission, release verification and durable 1.9 completion receipt must pass.
